primitives.note: Fury is a capped resource built by basic attacks (+5), crits/kills (+10), stacking additively per instance, decaying at 5/s after 8s without dealing/taking damage; drives the crit-chance conversion.
Current Fury (0-100) is converted directly into critical strike chance (0-50%), i.e. Fury is a proxy resource that ultimately buffs crit chance/damage.

Tryndamere has no innate base crit; all crit chance comes from Fury via P. Q's cast-timing note (crit roll locked in at windup start, before a mid-windup Bloodlust cast) and E's crit-triggered cooldown refund both depend on this crit chance.
Bloodlust's passive grants bonus AD scaling linearly with Tryndamere's missing health, capped at 90% missing health.
Bloodlust's active consumes 100% of current Fury; casting it zeroes the Fury pool and therefore Fury-derived crit chance, trading crit/damage potential for a heal (heal itself is defensive-only).
On-hit critical strikes reduce Spinning Slash's current cooldown by 0.75s (1.5s vs champions), stacking with normal cooldown countdown.
Spinning Slash deals a single instance of physical damage (base + 100% bonus AD + 80% AP) to each enemy hit by the dash, on a fixed cooldown.

Spinning Slash's hit depends on dash geometry (max 660 range, 225 hit radius, cast-at-max-range if out of range); a stationary single-target dummy fight must assume Tryndamere dashes onto/through the dummy every cast.

Reduces the target's bonus AD (and slows if facing away) for 4s; irrelevant to the damage-dealing (Tryndamere-attacks-dummy) fight since the dummy never attacks, but reduces damage taken from Tryndamere's target in the survival fight when Tryndamere is the tanky side attacked by a champion... actually here W is cast BY Tryndamere, so it only matters if Tryndamere is the survival-fight tank being hit by a champion and can reach/cast W on the attacker to reduce incoming damage.
Undying Rage instantly grants a flat burst of Fury (50/75/100), which feeds directly into the P crit-chance conversion.

Bloodlust's heal (min/max heal formulas) and Undying Rage's minimum-health-threshold/duration are never read by the damage-only dummy fight; they matter only for Tryndamere's own survivability in the survival fight.

needsBespoke.why: Tryndamere's entire crit chance is generated dynamically by a shared Fury resource that is built by attacks/crits/kills/E-hits/R, decays after 8s of inactivity, and can be entirely zeroed out by casting Q. Correctly simulating damage requires modeling this closed loop (attack -> Fury -> crit chance -> expected crit damage -> more Fury) tick-by-tick across the 15s window, plus E's on-crit cooldown refunds feeding back into cast frequency, and the timing quirk where a mid-windup Bloodlust cast uses the pre-cast crit chance but grants Fury only after the windup completes. This is more than the closed-list primitives can express as independent, composable effects; it needs bespoke stateful simulation of the Fury/crit feedback loop.

unsettled.question: Bloodlust's passive AD scales with Tryndamere's missing health, but in the damage-fight the dummy never damages Tryndamere, so his missing health stays at (or very near) 0 for the whole 15s. Should the simulator treat this passive as contributing ~0 bonus AD for the entire damage fight, or assume some non-zero missing-health baseline?
options: Compute missing health as 0 throughout, so the passive contributes 0 AD in the damage fight (literal reading of the fight rules)
Assume a fixed/average missing-health value (e.g. some percent) to approximate realistic play
Treat the passive AD term as not applicable to the damage-fight simulation at all

Which is correct for computing crit chance during the fight?
options: Flat conversion regardless of level, as stated on the wiki (0.5% crit per Fury point, cap 50%)
Conversion coefficient scales with champion level per the unexplained bin formula
The bin term is unrelated to the crit conversion (e.g. a different, unused passive value)

proposal: Open by auto-attacking the dummy immediately to start generating Fury (5 per hit, more on crits) since Tryndamere has zero Fury and zero crit chance at fight start.
Cast Spinning Slash (E) as soon as it is available (no cast time) to land a large upfront physical-damage instance, generate 5 Fury (champion target), and start its cooldown-refund-on-crit loop.

Cast Undying Rage (R) early for its instant Fury gain (50-100 depending on rank) purely to spike Fury-derived crit chance sooner, since its defensive minimum-health-threshold effect is not read in the damage fight.
Continue auto-attacking between E casts; recast Spinning Slash on cooldown, with cooldown further shortened by any on-hit crits landed since its last cast.

Do not cast Bloodlust (Q): consuming 100% of current Fury would zero out Fury-derived crit chance (reducing subsequent auto-attack and E damage) for a heal that the damage fight never rewards, and its passive AD bonus is near-zero since the dummy deals no damage back.
Do not cast Mocking Shout (W) in the damage fight: it only reduces the target's own AD, which a non-attacking dummy never uses, so it deals and enables no extra damage.

In the survival fight, is Tryndamere expected to spend actions casting Mocking Shout on the attacking champion for its AD-reduction/slow, or does the fixed enemy rotation make that impractical to model?
Does the simulator's crit-chance model apply Fury-derived crit multiplicatively/additively with any itemized crit chance, and is total crit chance capped at 100% as normal?
